meaning: to have the same understanding or agree about something
example: Before we launch the new app, let's make sure everyone is on the same page.
origin: Comes from people following the same page of a document or book during a meeting or lesson

wrong_meanings.meaning: to read the same book at the same time
wrong_meanings.why_wrong: This is the literal meaning of the words, not the idiomatic one.
The idiom is about agreement or understanding, not about owning or using the same technology.
The idiom has nothing to do with speed or rushing.

explanation: 'Be on the same page' means that people understand a situation in the same way and agree about what to do next. It is common in work meetings and team discussions.
